messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] streaming.p99 (eu-west) > 3.0s for 5m. Auto-page INC-20260315-91. See: https://console.redwood.ai/d/streams/slo

raj: ack. I'm oncall. Pulling up proxy write queues and connection table. p95 stable ~300ms, p99 ~3.2-4.0s. streaming-proxy-eu-2 showing long write buffers.

sara: noticing a pattern: ~4 clients from cust-993 are at TCP RCV window 0 for long periods, which makes upstream writes pile up. client-windowing metric jumped.

marc: envoy metrics show downstream_flush_failures and upstream_too_many_pending_requests. Could be slow-consumer (client not reading) causing head-of-line stalls.

emily: mitigation options: A) heartbeat to force periodic flush + small keepalive B) evict idle/slow clients with server-side reset for offending org C) temporarily route troubled org traffic to non-streaming fallback. Which do we prefer?

raj: do A+B in parallel. Heartbeat first (low risk), then targeted eviction for cust-993 connections older than 30s and zero bytes read. I'll prepare the evict command.

marc: also propose increasing proxy_write_timeout from 20s -> 45s on canary to avoid cascading connection resets during rollout. I'll open canary patch.

ops-deploy-bot: starting canary deploy for proxy-config-eu (patch id can-1783004) to streaming-proxy-eu-2.

raj: enabling heartbeat flag: `PATCH /flags/streaming/heartbeat_interval {"interval_ms":15000}` -> 200 OK. Heartbeats rolling to proxies.

sara: heartbeats landing. I'm starting targeted eviction for cust-993 now: `POST /admin/evict-sessions?org=cust-993&age_gt=30s&bytes_read=0` -> job evict-1783 started.

support-bot: Ticket SUP-20260315-1012 created for cust-993. Notified AE and support lead.

marc: canary config applied, upstream timeout set to 45s on one proxy node. Monitoring queue lengths.

raj: eviction job reports ~620 sessions terminated across 4 frontends. Immediate p99 drop to ~900ms on those proxies. Region p99 trending to 1.1s.

emily: seeing residual 502s on chunked fallback for legacy clients; looks like chunk boundary negotiation fails when multipart headers exist. I'll add a header-skip in the fallback proxy.

raj: patched fallback proxy to strip X-Client-Bulk and X-Stream-Meta for chunked path. Patch rolled to 15% traffic. Errors dropped.

ops-deploy-bot: canary roll finished. config rollout id roll-1783004.

pagerduty-bot: PD note: INC-20260315-91 acknowledged by raj; emily on watch handoff scheduled in 30m if stable.

katie: customer impact analysis: cust-993 had 2.8% of region streams and experienced stalls starting 11:18 UTC. Estimated affected sessions ~1.2k, peak reconnections ~420. AE and support on the case.

marc: after fixes p99 ~1.0-1.4s, p95 ~270-340ms. Queue depth normalized. No continued surge in new slow-consumer sessions.

raj: rolling a small follow-up: implement per-org connection-slope alert (rate of increase > 50 connections/min) and an automatic slow-client eviction policy for >60s of zero-read with thresh 500 concurrent. Will file infra ticket.

emily: taking over watch. Handoff: raj -> emily. I've captured trace ids: trace-eu-1783-az1 and trace-eu-1783-az2. Links on incident page.

support-bot: Created post-incident support summary: https://support.redwood.ai/cases/SUP-20260315-1012 with customer timeline.

raj: quick notes for postmortem: root cause = concentrated slow-consumer connections from a single customer + proxy timeouts not tuned for writeback pressure leading to long-tail p99 amplification. Successful mitigations = heartbeat flush + targeted eviction + strip headers for chunked fallback. Long-term actions: per-org slope alert, automatic eviction, and client SDK guidance for windowing.

emily: will own P1 follow-ups and coordinate with platform and customer success. If things recur tag @emily and escalate. thanks all :thumbsup:
